title: Sound
seo_title: Sound Class 9 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 11)
standard_text: Sound: Nature of sound and its propagation in various media, speed of sound, range of hearing in humans; ultrasound; reflection of sound; echo.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 9 Science worksheets for NCERT Chapter 11: how sound is produced and travels, compressions and rarefactions, v = fλ, pitch and loudness, the range of hearing, echo, reverberation, ultrasound and SONAR. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: For an echo, the sound travels twice the distance.
body_html:
How to think about it

Sound is made by vibrating objects and travels as a longitudinal wave of compressions and rarefactions through a medium; it cannot travel through a vacuum. It is fastest in solids and slowest in gases. Its speed is v = fλ, and the time period is T = 1 ÷ f. Frequency sets the pitch and amplitude sets the loudness.

Sound reflects from hard surfaces; an echo is heard if the reflector is at least about 17 m away. Humans hear 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz; higher frequencies are ultrasound, used in SONAR and medical scans. In echo problems, distance = speed × time ÷ 2.

Example

f = 500 Hz, λ = 0.68 m. Speed?

v = fλ

Answer: 340 m/s

Example

Echo after 2 s, v = 340 m/s. Distance?

2d = 340 × 2

Answer: 340 m

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to halve the distance in echo and SONAR problems.
  • Mixing up pitch (frequency) and loudness (amplitude).
  • Saying sound travels faster in air than in water.

faq.q: Why can we not hear sound on the Moon?
faq.a: There is no air (no medium) to carry the sound waves.

faq.q: What is the difference between an echo and reverberation?
faq.a: An echo is a single reflected sound heard separately; reverberation is the sound lasting in a hall because of many repeated reflections.
